The marketing site should therefore not expose the URL until the owner says the app is live.

FLAG FOR THE OWNER (outside the marketing site): if the owner does not want orders yet, they should ask the app's developer to do one of two things:
(a) Put the form into a closed state server-side. The app already has a built-in message, \"אין כרגע מוצרים להזמנה דרך האתר. אפשר להזמין בטלפון.\" (inference: shown when no products are open for web ordering).
(b) Add X-Robots-Tag: noindex or Cloudflare Access to /order until launch.
Either way, they should confirm that no stray orders have arrived. We did not test submission.

HOW THE MARKETING SITE SHOULD LINK WHILE THE APP IS NOT LIVE:
1. Keep one config value, e.g. orderApp = { status: 'soon' | 'live', url: 'https://haofeapp.com/order', branch: 'netivot' }. Every order call-to-action reads from it. Set it by hand. Do not detect status automatically: /order returns 200 whether or not the owner considers it live, so an HTTP check cannot tell the difference.
2. While status is 'soon':
   - Show a non-clickable badge such as \"הזמנה אונליין – בקרוב\". Use a span or a disabled button, not an <a href>.
   - Put the URL nowhere: not in the HTML, sitemap, JSON-LD (no potentialAction/OrderAction), Open Graph tags or link previews. This keeps crawlers and customers from finding it through our site.
   - Make the primary actions the ones that work today: phone tel:+97289752093 for Netivot, plus Waze.
3. Optional, recommended: create a stable short link on the marketing domain, e.g. /order or /הזמנה, that shows a coming-soon page with the phone numbers. That link can go on flyers, QR codes and the Instagram bio now. At launch it becomes a 302 redirect to https://haofeapp.com/order, and rolling back means flipping it back. Nothing printed ever has to change.

HOW TO SWITCH ON LATER:
- Only after the owner confirms launch and has run a test order themselves (WhatsApp confirmation and staff dashboard working), set status to 'live'. The badge then becomes a real link to exactly https://haofeapp.com/order. Use https, no trailing slash (the slash form causes a 308 redirect), not www (no DNS record) and not the root URL (that is the staff login).
- Link normally, in the same tab or with target=_blank rel=noopener. Never use an iframe: the app sends x-frame-options: DENY.
- UTM parameters (e.g. ?utm_source=site&utm_medium=cta) are probably harmless, but check with the developer, because the app ends its referrer at same-origin and may not record them.
- Add JSON-LD potentialAction (OrderAction, target https://haofeapp.com/order) to the Netivot Bakery/LocalBusiness entry only.

SCOPE AND COPY RULES THAT MATCH THE APP:
- The app covers Netivot only and pickup only (\"איסוף עצמי בלבד\"). Show the order button only on the Netivot branch card, labelled something like \"הזמנה לאיסוף מסניף נתיבות\". Sderot and Kiryat Gat cards keep phone-only contact. Kiryat Gat has no confirmed phone number, so do not invent one.
- Do not promise delivery.
- Friday orders are phone-only (08-9752093). Web orders run up to 30 days ahead and at least 2 hours before pickup.
- The app lists Netivot hours (א׳–ה׳ 05:00–22:00, שישי 05:00–15:00, מוצאי שבת 20:00–23:00). Confirm them with the owner before publishing.
- When the app expands to more branches, change the single branch value in the config to a list rather than hard-coding links.

www.haofeapp.com has no DNS record (NXDOMAIN), so there was nothing to load.

By the read-only rules I did not submit a test order, POST to /api/order-requests, or log in at the staff screen. Whether the server currently accepts and processes public orders is therefore unknown.

requirements.topic: 1. Distance-sale disclosure before the order (section 14ג(א), Consumer Protection Law)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: In remote marketing (שיווק מרחוק) the business must disclose at least: (1) its name, ID/company number and address in Israel and abroad; (2) the main features of the goods; (3) the price and the available payment terms; (4) when and how the goods will be supplied; (5) how long the offer is valid; (6) warranty details; (7) details of the consumer's cancellation right under 14ג(ג) or 14ג1(ג). The definition of 'שיווק מרחוק' in 14ג(ו) covers an approach to a consumer by mail, telephone or any electronic communication, or through catalogues or ads, aimed at a transaction where the parties are not together in person. The Nevo consolidated text is current as of 30-09-2026; I viewed it on 2026-10-24 and read the full wording in the Wikisource copy. MY INFERENCE: the app/web ordering flow is distance marketing. Any phone or WhatsApp ordering line advertised today (the Instagram bio snippet mentions an ordering line) probably already triggers 14ג.
requirements.applies_when: Before the order is placed, on the product, cart or checkout screens of haofeapp.com/order, and for any phone or WhatsApp ordering that is advertised.

requirements.topic: 1. Written confirmation after the order (14ג(ב)) and business identity (4ב)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: In a distance sale the business must give the consumer a written document, in Hebrew or in the language used for the marketing, no later than the time of supply. It must contain: identity and main features (per (א)(1)-(2)); the price and the payment terms that apply; how to exercise the cancellation right; the manufacturer's name and country of manufacture; warranty information; and other terms of the deal. Separately, section 4ב requires the business's name and ID number on order forms, offers, contracts, credit slips and tax invoices. MY INFERENCE: an order-confirmation email or SMS plus the receipt can carry these details. The legal entity (name and ח.פ.) behind the app has to be confirmed.
requirements.applies_when: For every order made through the app or by phone, no later than delivery or pickup.

requirements.topic: 2. Cancellation right and the perishable-goods exemption (14ג(ג)-(ד))
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: In a distance sale of goods, the consumer may cancel from the day of the deal until 14 days after receiving the goods or the 14ג(ב) document, whichever is later. Under 14ג(ד), that right (and the extended 4-month right in 14ג1(ג) for people with disabilities, senior citizens and new immigrants) does not apply to: (1) perishable goods (טובין פסידים); (4) goods made specially for the consumer following the deal; and some other categories that are not relevant here. MY INFERENCE: fresh bread and pastries are perishable, and custom or personalised cakes are 'made specially', so both are likely excluded. Shelf-stable or non-food items may not be excluded (see the open questions).
requirements.applies_when: For all app orders. The exemption has to be assessed per product type.

requirements.topic: 2. תקנות הגנת הצרכן (ביטול עסקה), התשע"א-2010: food exclusion and scope
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: Regulation 6(א) excludes from the cancellation right, among other items, (4) food products (מוצרי מזון) and (6) perishable goods (טובין פסידים). 'Goods' means goods for which more than NIS 50 was paid (reg. 1). Nevo shows the text as current on 18-09-2023. The regulations were made under section 14ו, which covers specified goods and services. A Chamber of Commerce legal note (secondary, https://www.chamber.org.il/serviceslobby/legal/1857/106277/, seen only as a search snippet) says these regulations govern in-person store transactions, while distance-sale cancellation is governed by 14ג. MY INFERENCE: for app orders the operative exemption is 14ג(ד)(1). The regulations' food exclusion matters mainly for purchases made in the branches.
requirements.applies_when: Mainly in-branch purchases. Cited for app orders only as background.

requirements.topic: 2. Refunds and cancellation fees where cancellation is allowed (14ה)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: If a consumer cancels under 14ג(ג) because of a defect, a mismatch with the disclosed details, non-supply on the agreed date or another breach, the business must refund within 14 days of the cancellation notice, cancel the charge, and may not take any cancellation fee. If the consumer cancels for any other reason, the business must refund within 14 days and may keep a cancellation fee of no more than 5% of the price or NIS 100, whichever is lower. 'Cancellation fee' includes shipping and packing costs (14ה(ד)). MY INFERENCE: this matters only for items that are not perishable and not custom-made.
requirements.applies_when: Non-exempt items sold through the app, e.g. possibly packaged shelf-stable goods, gift boxes, merchandise or vouchers (to be checked).

requirements.topic: 2. 'No cancellation' wording must be qualified (2(ב2)); return-policy sign (4ג)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: A business that announces in any way that the consumer has no right to cancel or to a refund must qualify the announcement so that it is clear it does not apply in cases set by law (2(ב2)). The in-store return-policy notice duty in 4ג does not apply to food products or perishable goods (4ג(ד)(1)). MY INFERENCE: app terms should not say only 'no cancellations'. They should name the excluded categories and carry the statutory qualification.
requirements.applies_when: In the app's cancellation policy, terms of use (תקנון) and checkout text.

requirements.topic: 3. Price display: only the total price, in shekels, including delivery (17א, 17ב, 17ד, 14ג(ו))
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: 'המחיר הכולל' (the total price) includes VAT, levies, and any other payment that comes with the purchase and that the consumer has no practical way to waive (17א). Goods offered or displayed must show only the total price, only in Israeli currency, visibly and legibly; the displayed price is binding even if checkout shows more (17ב). A business may not advertise or quote a price unless it is the total price in shekels (17ד). For distance sales, 'מחיר הנכס' is the total price including delivery fees and any other addition or expense the consumer will bear (14ג(ו)).
requirements.applies_when: Every price shown in the app, on the marketing site, or in a coming-soon notice.

requirements.topic: 3. Unit price (per kg or per 100 g) in distance sales
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: תקנות הגנת הצרכן (מחיר ליחידת מידה), התשס"ח-2008 apply to all distance sales whatever the store size (reg. 6(א)). In a distance sale the unit price must appear right next to the item price (reg. 3(ב)). The duty covers goods sold in bulk and pre-packed goods that must state their quantity by law or official standard (reg. 2(א)). Packaged food under 1 kg is priced per 100 g (reg. 2(ב)). Exemptions in reg. 6(ב) include 'לחם לא ארוז לסוגיו' (unpackaged bread of all kinds), items weighing 100 g or less (unless made in several weights), mixed packs, and items whose unit price equals the total price. Nevo shows the text as current on 18-09-2023.
requirements.applies_when: App listings of pre-packed items with a stated net weight, or items sold by weight. Unpackaged bread is exempt.

requirements.topic: 3. No minimum purchase for paying by card (12א)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: A business that accepts debit or credit cards may not make card payment conditional on a minimum purchase amount (section 12א, added in תשפ"ה). I read this text in the Wikisource copy of the law. I did not check it separately on the Nevo page, which shows the consolidated law as current on 30-09-2026.
requirements.applies_when: If the app sets a minimum order amount. Whether a payment-neutral minimum for delivery is allowed is an open question.

requirements.topic: 3. Delivery fees shown only at checkout: enforcement signal
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: An ice.co.il article dated 12/5/2025 describes a class-action claim against a food chain alleging that the delivery or pickup fee appeared only at the virtual checkout. The claim relied on the total-price rule and on a 'הנחיית הממונה על הגנת הצרכן בנוגע להצגת מחירים בעסקאות מכר מרחוק' (Commissioner's directive on price display in distance sales). I could not find the text or date of that directive. MY INFERENCE: show delivery and packing fees early, at the latest when the first item goes into the cart.
requirements.applies_when: App cart and checkout design.

requirements.topic: 4. Delivery and pickup timing disclosure
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: Before the deal, the business must disclose when and how the goods will be supplied, and how long the offer is valid (14ג(א)(4)-(5)). Misleading the consumer about the supply date, or about the place where the goods will be supplied, is misleading on a material matter (2(א)(3), (3א)). If the consumer paid in advance and, for reasons the seller is responsible for, the goods are not supplied within two weeks of the agreed date (or within two months of payment if no date was agreed), the business owes interest (13(ב)). MY INFERENCE: give realistic delivery or pickup windows per branch. For perishable orders, cancellation and refund for late delivery rest on general contract law, because 14ג(ג) does not apply (lawyer to confirm).
requirements.applies_when: Every app order with delivery or branch pickup.

requirements.topic: 4. Delivery-area policy (תקנות הגנת הצרכן (גילוי פרט מהותי לגבי אספקת נכס או שירות), התשע"ח-2018)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: A business selling goods for which delivery is offered, even if the consumer can decline delivery, must disclose before the deal whether there are places it does not deliver to, and what restrictions apply to delivery there (reg. 2(א)). In a distance sale this must be disclosed at the marketing stage, in a prominent place, in clear and legible letters and figures (reg. 2(ג)(3)). Nevo shows the text as current on 18-09-2023. Note: the separate 2015 regulations on delivery services (גילוי פרט מהותי לגבי שירות משלוח טובין) apply only to a 'משלח' that ships goods from abroad into Israel, so they are not relevant here.
requirements.applies_when: If the app offers delivery from the Netivot, Sderot or Kiryat Gat branches.

requirements.topic: 5. Ingredients and allergens: general duties under the Consumer Protection Law
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: The ingredients (המרכיבים) of a product, and the risks of using it, are listed as material matters on which misleading is prohibited (2(א)(2), (4)). A business must disclose any feature of a product that requires special handling or use to prevent harm to the user (4(א)(2)). MY INFERENCE: wrong or missing allergen information in the app (e.g. 'nut-free' when there is cross-contact risk) can count as misleading. Section 4(א)(2) could arguably extend to known allergens. The second point is my interpretation, not a stated rule.
requirements.applies_when: Any product description, ingredient list or allergen tag in the app.

requirements.topic: 5. Food labelling regime: EU Regulation 1169/2011 adopted in Israel
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: In a notice dated 19.2.2026, the Ministry of Health states that Regulation (EU) 1169/2011 (food information to consumers) was adopted by Amendment 10 to the Food Law (חוק הגנה על בריאות הציבור (מזון), התשע"ו-2015) and appears as item 5 of Schedule 2א. It has applied voluntarily, subject to conditions, since 1 January 2025, and is expected to apply to all businesses from 1 January 2028. Food-specific local labelling rules, including those that refer to ת"י 1145 (labelling of pre-packed food), continue to apply. The notice sets a temporary administrative enforcement policy from 18.2.2026.
requirements.applies_when: Pre-packed products the bakery makes (the Netivot production plant) and sells online or in branches.

requirements.topic: 5. Food information in distance selling (Art. 14 of 1169/2011) and Israeli changes
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCES SAY: Article 14 of 1169/2011 (EU text at https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2011/1169) requires that, for pre-packed food sold by distance communication, the mandatory food information (except the durability date) be available before the purchase is concluded; for non-pre-packed food it refers to the Article 44 particulars. In Israel, Schedule 2א item 5 to the Food Law (as transcribed on Wikisource) says Article 44(1)(a), the EU duty to give allergen information for non-pre-packed food, is not read in Israel for seven years from 1.1.2025 (a temporary provision). It also adds a mandatory fava-bean (פול) warning for G6PD deficiency. MY INFERENCE: until 2028, online allergen display for unpackaged baked goods has no specific statutory basis found. From 2028, pre-packed items sold online will probably need full label information before purchase. Showing allergens now is prudent.
requirements.applies_when: App product pages, especially pre-packed items. Unpackaged items depend on how Art. 44 is read in Israel.

requirements.topic: 5. Nutrition 'red symbols' when selling pre-packed food online
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCES SAY: תקנות הגנה על בריאות הציבור (מזון) (סימון תזונתי), התשע"ח-2017 place the nutrition-labelling duty, including red symbols, on manufacturers and importers of pre-packed food. Their definition of pre-packed food excludes food prepared at the consumer's request at the time of sale. A Chamber of Commerce note dated 01/12/2019 reports that the Consumer Protection Commissioner treats product details as material in online sales and gave online retailers a transition period, attaching a guidance dated 25.12.19. I could not see the official guidance text. MY INFERENCE: if an app item carries red symbols on its pack, show them on the product page.
requirements.applies_when: Pre-packed items with red symbols listed in the app.

requirements.topic: 6. Privacy: Amendment 13 and the notice duty (section 11)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCES SAY: Amendment 13 to חוק הגנת הפרטיות came into force on 14.8.2025 (Privacy Protection Authority guide). Any request to a person for personal information to be processed in a database must come with a notice stating: (1) whether there is a legal duty to provide the information or it depends on the person's consent, and what happens if they refuse; (2) the purpose; (2א) the name and contact details of the database controller; (3) to whom the information will be passed and for what purposes; (4) the right to inspect (s.13) and to request correction (s.14). Nevo shows the law as current on 11-10-2026. The PPA's position paper (https://www.gov.il/BlobFolder/legalinfo/duty_to_notify/he/notify13.pdf) says the duty applies to every channel, including online and oral, and also when data is collected because the person asked for a service.
requirements.applies_when: App sign-up and checkout, and any 'notify me' form on a coming-soon page.

requirements.topic: 6. Database registration and notice thresholds after Amendment 13 (8א)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: Registration is required only if (a) the database's main purpose is collecting personal data to pass to others as a business or for payment (including direct-mail services) and it holds data on more than 10,000 people, or (b) the controller is a public body. A controller of a database that does not need registration must notify the Authority within 30 days once it holds especially sensitive information (מידע בעל רגישות מיוחדת) on more than 100,000 people. Under the definition of 'מאגר מידע', a collection holding only name, address and contact details of up to 100,000 people is not a database, provided it reveals no other personal data and the owner holds no other collection with further details on the same people. MY INFERENCE: a bakery customer database will probably not need registration, but the section 11 notice and the data-security duties still apply.
requirements.applies_when: The customer database behind the app.

requirements.topic: 6. Especially sensitive information: allergy and health notes
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: 'מידע בעל רגישות מיוחדת' includes personal information about a person's health and information about their financial activity, among other categories. MY INFERENCE: a free-text order note such as 'my son has a nut allergy', or saved dietary or medical preferences, is health information. Collecting it raises the stakes (higher penalties apply where sensitive data is involved) and calls for minimisation and suitable security.
requirements.applies_when: If the app lets customers record allergies or dietary needs, or stores payment data itself.

requirements.topic: 6. Amendment 13 penalties and damages without proof of harm
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS (PPA guide, May 2025, viewed 2026-10-24): For collecting data without a proper section 11 notice, the administrative fine is NIS 50 per person approached, or NIS 100 per person where especially sensitive data is involved. The guide also states a NIS 30,000 minimum per breach; its layout leaves it unclear whether that minimum covers both cases. The guide's example: 5,000 people approached for sensitive data without notice gives NIS 500,000. Courts may award up to NIS 10,000 without proof of damage, for example for collecting data without the section 11 notice. Total fines are capped at 5% of annual turnover. Breaches of the Information Security Regulations (2017) also carry fines.
requirements.applies_when: Risk assessment for the app and for any coming-soon signup form.

requirements.topic: 6. Valid consent and marketing opt-in: PPA opinion of 25.2.2026
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: The Authority's opinion on consent (גילוי דעת בנושא הסכמה, 25.2.2026) says: silence or lack of objection is not valid consent; consent to one purpose does not allow use for another purpose without new consent; for direct-mail services and for marketing uses unrelated to the purpose of the deal, consent must be a separate active opt-in, not opt-out; documenting consent is recommended.
requirements.applies_when: Any marketing use of app or signup data.

requirements.topic: 6. Spam law: section 30א of חוק התקשורת (בזק ושידורים)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: Advertising by email, SMS, fax or auto-dialler requires the recipient's explicit prior consent, in writing (an electronic message or recorded call counts) (30א(ב)). Exception (30א(ג)): the recipient gave their details during a purchase or negotiation, was told the details would be used for advertising, was given a chance to refuse and did not, and the ad concerns similar products. The recipient may refuse at any time, free of charge (30א(ד)). Each ad must clearly show: the word 'פרסומת' at its start, and in the subject line of an email; the advertiser's name, address and contact details; and the right to opt out, with a simple way to do it (for email, a valid address for opting out) (30א(ה)). Courts may award up to NIS 1,000 per message without proof of damage, and knowledge is presumed (30א(י)). I read the full text on Wikisource (https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/חוק_התקשורת_(בזק_ושידורים)); the Nevo page lists amendments up to Amendment 83 of 28.7.2026, but I did not see section 30א's body there.
requirements.applies_when: Launch-announcement emails or SMS, newsletters, promotional SMS from the app.

requirements.topic: 6. Direct-mail approaches (17ו) and DPO duty (17ב1)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: 'דיוור ישיר' means a personal approach to someone based on their belonging to a group defined by one or more characteristics of the people in a database. Every direct-mail approach must clearly state that it is direct mail, together with the registration number of the database used for direct-mail services, the right to be deleted, and the controller's identity and data sources (17ו). The PPA guide lists breaches of 17ו(א) as subject to fines. Appointing a privacy officer (DPO) is mandatory for public bodies, data brokers over 10,000 people, large-scale systematic monitoring, and large-scale processing of sensitive data (17ב1). MY INFERENCE: a bakery is probably not required to appoint a DPO. How 17ו applies to the bakery's own segmented marketing from a database that does not need registration is unclear.
requirements.applies_when: Segmented marketing, e.g. by branch or purchase history.

requirements.topic: 7. Accessibility of the website and online ordering (regs 35, 35א)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: 'שירות אינטרנט' covers content of any format delivered over the internet through websites, documents or applications that provide a service to the public or information about it (reg. 35). A service provider must make its internet services accessible under ת"י 5568 (the Israeli web accessibility standard, 'as amended from time to time') at level AA (reg. 35א(א)). Forms used to receive a service must comply (35א(ג)(2)). A deviation is treated as a breach only if the business was notified and did not fix it within a reasonable time, at most 60 days, and alternative access must be given in the meantime (35א(ד)). Third-party content is exempt, but the platform must be accessible (35ב).
requirements.applies_when: The marketing site, the coming-soon notice, and haofeapp.com/order, unless an exemption applies.

requirements.topic: 7. Mobile apps (35ג), accessibility statement (35ה) and exemptions (35ו)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: Apps for smartphones and tablets must meet an Israeli app standard if one exists. If none exists, they must meet the relevant success criteria of the web standard as far as the operating system allows, on at least two common operating systems (35ג(ב)). An app is exempt if an identical service runs on an accessible mobile-adapted website, and the app links to it (35ג(ג)). The website and the app must each show, in a prominent place, an accessibility statement: the adjustments made, the accessibility coordinator's details if one is required, and contact details for reporting problems (35ה). Exempt: an עוסק פטור (VAT-exempt dealer), or a business whose average annual turnover is no more than NIS 100,000 (35ו(ז)). A technical-infeasibility exemption is available through an accessibility officer and must be published in the statement (35ו(א)-(ג)).
requirements.applies_when: If a native app is released, and for the accessibility statement on the site and the app.

requirements.topic: 7. Current edition of ת"י 5568
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: The Standards Institution page lists ת"י 5568 part 1, 'קווים מנחים לנגישות תכנים באינטרנט: נגישות אתרי אינטרנט', published 28/09/2023 (Reshumot publication 22/10/2023), replacing the 2021 part 1. The page does not say which WCAG version it is based on. Downloadable digital documents are covered by part 2. MY INFERENCE: because reg. 35 refers to the standard 'as amended from time to time', the 2023 edition is the benchmark.
requirements.applies_when: Design and audit of the site and the app.

requirements.topic: 7. Damages without proof of harm for accessibility breaches
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: Section 19נא of חוק שוויון זכויות לאנשים עם מוגבלות makes breaches of the accessibility provisions a civil wrong. Courts may award up to NIS 50,000 without proof of damage for listed breaches, with defences such as an existing accessibility order or undertaking. I did not confirm which listed section covers the internet-service regulations; I read the text on Wikisource.
requirements.applies_when: Risk assessment if the site or app is not accessible.

requirements.topic: Coming soon: misleading-advertising rules (sections 2 and 7)
requirements.requirement: WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: A business may not do anything, by act or omission, in writing, orally or otherwise, that may mislead a consumer on a material matter. Material matters include the supply date, the place of supply, the price usually charged, and cancellation terms (2(א)(3), (3א), (13), (21)). Whoever the advertising is made for is liable for misleading advertising (7(א)). The Commissioner may demand evidence for factual claims in an ad, and failing to provide it is prima facie evidence that the ad misled (7(ב)). MY INFERENCE: a 'coming soon' notice is advertising, so launch dates, prices, promotions, delivery areas and features stated in it must be true and supportable.
requirements.applies_when: Coming-soon banners, posts and the haofeapp.com/order placeholder page.

coming_soon_guidance: Say plainly that ordering in the app is not open yet, for example: 'בקרוב: הזמנות אונליין באפליקציה של האופה. האפליקציה עדיין לא פעילה ולא ניתן להזמין בה כרגע.' This is my inference from section 2: implying a live service is misleading. Draft wording, for lawyer review.

Do not promise a launch date ('next week', 'November 1') unless it is firm. The supply or service date is a material matter under 2(א)(3), and 7(ב) lets the Commissioner demand proof of advertised facts. If the owner wants a timeframe, a lawyer should approve the wording.

Do not show prices, 'launch discounts' or 'regular price X, now Y' claims for the app. Any price that is shown must be the total price in NIS, including VAT and any unavoidable fee (17א, 17ד), and the business must be ready to honour it. A reference price is a material matter (2(א)(13)). Safest: no prices on the coming-soon notice.

Do not take orders, payments, deposits or pre-orders through the placeholder, and do not show 'order now' buttons that look active. Any real pre-order would be a distance sale with full 14ג disclosures, and paid deposits can trigger interest under 13(ב). Disable or hide the /order route until it is live, or show only the notice there.

Do not state delivery areas, delivery times or branch coverage (for example 'delivery to all of Netivot, Sderot and Kiryat Gat') unless confirmed. The place and date of supply are material matters (2(א)(3), (3א)), and the 2018 regulations require disclosure of areas not covered once delivery is offered.

Do not advertise app features that may not exist at launch, such as allergen filters, 'kosher lemehadrin at all branches', loyalty points or app-store availability. Show App Store or Google Play badges only once the app is actually published there. This is my inference from sections 2 and 7. Kashrut claims per branch also need checking against the certificates (see the open questions).

If the notice points people to current ordering channels (for example a branch phone or WhatsApp), remember those are themselves distance sales. The 14ג(א) disclosures (identity, price, supply time and method, cancellation details with the 2(ב2) qualification) already apply to them.

A 'notify me when it launches' form is optional. If used, collect the minimum (one contact field) and show a section 11 notice next to it. Draft wording for lawyer review: 'מסירת הפרטים אינה חובה ותלויה בהסכמתך; בלי הפרטים לא נוכל לעדכן אותך. הפרטים ישמשו רק כדי להודיע לך שהאפליקציה עלתה. בעל השליטה במאגר: [שם משפטי, ח.פ., כתובת, דוא"ל]. הפרטים יועברו ל[ספק הדיוור] לצורך המשלוח בלבד. יש לך זכות לעיין במידע ולבקש לתקנו (סעיפים 13-14 לחוק הגנת הפרטיות).' Link to a full privacy policy. Do not collect allergy or health details at this stage.

Treat the launch-announcement message itself as advertising under 30א. Get explicit prior consent through an unticked checkbox, for example 'אני מסכים/ה לקבל מהאופה הודעה על השקת האפליקציה ודברי פרסומת בדוא"ל/SMS'. Keep that checkbox separate from any terms acceptance (PPA opinion 25.2.2026: separate opt-in; consent for one purpose does not cover another). In the message, put 'פרסומת' at the start or in the subject line, give the sender's name, address and contact details, and include a working opt-out. Log each consent with its date and the text shown.

Use signup data only for the stated purpose. Using it later for general marketing, profiling or passing it to a franchisee or platform needs its own notice and consent (s.11; s.8(ב) purpose limitation; PPA consent opinion).

Analytics or ad pixels on the coming-soon page: I found no Israeli statute specific to cookies. The PPA opinion says silence or continued use is not valid consent, and secondary sources read it as requiring consent for non-essential tracking. Keep the placeholder free of non-essential trackers, or get a lawyer's view first.

The coming-soon notice is part of the website, so it must meet ת"י 5568 level AA (reg. 35א): real text rather than text baked into an image, sufficient contrast, alt text, a keyboard-usable and labelled signup form, and readable RTL Hebrew. The site needs an accessibility statement (35ה), unless the business is an עוסק פטור or its average turnover is no more than NIS 100,000 (35ו(ז)).

Keep a dated copy of what the coming-soon notice and any signup form said, and when. This is my inference: it supports the evidential burden under 7(ב) and lets you show the consent text if a 30א claim is made.
open_questions_for_lawyer: Which bakery items fall outside the 14ג(ד) exemptions (perishable; made specially for the consumer)? For example: shelf-stable packaged cookies or crackers, gift boxes, merchandise, gift cards or vouchers, and catering trays ordered days ahead. Those items would carry a 14-day cancellation right with a fee capped at the lower of 5% or NIS 100 (14ה).

Is an order placed in the app but picked up at a branch a 'עסקת מכר מרחוק'? (I infer yes, because the contract is formed remotely.) Should the app allow voluntary cancellation before the order is prepared, and on what terms, given 14ג(ג) does not apply to perishables?

For perishable orders that arrive late or not at all, what remedies apply and what refund timing should the policy promise, given that 14ה(א) refers to cancellation under 14ג(ג), which is excluded for perishables?
Does a minimum order amount for delivery that applies to every payment method conflict with section 12א (ban on a minimum purchase for card payment)?

Please obtain the text and date of the Consumer Protection Commissioner's directive on price display in distance sales (cited in the May 2025 class action reported by ice.co.il). In particular: must delivery or packing fees appear on product pages, or is the first cart view enough?

Unit pricing: which of the bakery's online items are 'pre-packed goods that must state quantity'? Does the exemption for 'לחם לא ארוז לסוגיו' cover unpackaged pastries, rolls and cakes, or only bread?

Allergens: is there any current Israeli duty to show allergens online for non-pre-packed bakery goods? Wikisource's copy of Food Law Schedule 2א item 5 says Art. 44(1)(a) of 1169/2011 is 'not read' for seven years from 1.1.2025; please confirm against the official text and the Ministry of Health's Hebrew translation. What exactly will Art. 14 (distance selling) require from 1.1.2028 for the bakery's pre-packed products?

Is the bakery the licensed manufacturer (the Netivot plant at הסוללים 1 appears in the Badatz Beit Yosef listing as a factory), and are its packaged products labelled under ת"י 1145 or 1169/2011? This decides what the app must reproduce on product pages, including red symbols.

Kashrut: under חוק איסור הונאה בכשרות, what kashrut statements may the app make per branch and per product? The Badatz listing found earlier covers the Netivot factory; whether the Sderot and Kiryat Gat branches hold certificates was not checked.

Who is the legal entity that operates the app (name, ח.פ./ID, address) across the three branches? Are any branches franchises? This affects identity disclosure (14ג(א)(1), 4ב), where refunds are made, and who the database controller is.

Privacy setup: Is the customer database a 'מאגר מידע' in light of the 100,000 contact-only exception and any other customer data held? Which security level applies under תקנות הגנת הפרטיות (אבטחת מידע), 2017? What processor ('מחזיק') agreement is needed with the ordering platform, payment provider and SMS/email vendor? Should allergy notes be collected at all?
Does 17ו (direct-mail disclosures, including a registration number) apply to the bakery's own segmented marketing from a database that does not need registration after Amendment 13?
Are app push notifications and WhatsApp marketing messages 'electronic messages' under 30א? What consent flow does the app need for them?

Accessibility: confirm the business is not exempt under 35ו(ז) (עוסק פטור or average turnover up to NIS 100,000). Is an accessibility coordinator required (the size threshold was not checked)? Which ת"י 5568 edition and WCAG version will an auditor apply? Does 19נא statutory compensation reach the internet-service regulations?
Can the app terms (תקנון) include limitation or arbitration clauses, given חוק החוזים האחידים and the font-size rules under section 4א? I did not research these.
